memory_update.text: MOD should remain in the thermal-management node as an underfollowed but increasingly visible AI data-center cooling candidate; key survival tests are data-center backlog conversion, customer concentration, capacity, and margins.

NVT is a liquid-cooling bill-of-materials candidate through CDUs, manifolds, rear-door heat exchangers, and rack-level infrastructure; evidence gap is materiality of AI liquid-cooling revenue versus legacy enclosures/electrical products.
SPXC is a second-order cooling and heat-rejection candidate with explicit data-center demand commentary, but needs segment-level proof before promotion beyond Layer 1.

Thermal-management chokepoint should be split into at least four subnodes in later layers: facility chillers and heat rejection, rack-level CDUs/manifolds/rear-door exchangers, direct-to-chip cold plates and coolant loops, and water/chemistry/digital monitoring services.

ECL was not included as a candidate due to large-cap breadth, but the pending CoolIT acquisition is a critical validation signal for the scarcity and strategic value of pure-play AI liquid-cooling assets.

node: Data-center thermal management, liquid cooling, chillers, CDUs, heat exchangers, pumps, valves, and controls
summary: Expanded the thermal-management and liquid-cooling node into a two-lane universe. Reference lane: Vertiv remains the obvious pure-play context anchor for high-density data-center thermal systems and CDUs. Underfollowed lane: Modine, nVent, and SPX Technologies have plausible direct or second-order exposure through AI data-center chillers, CDUs, rack liquid-cooling components, evaporative/heat-rejection equipment, and cooling products whose demand is increasingly tied to AI rack density. These are not trading recommendations; they are Layer 1B research candidates requiring backlog, customer, margin, capacity, and segment-disclosure verification.
